R638.note: Host allowlist plus relative-path allowance closes the redirect; java.net.URI rejects backslash tricks and the error message matches the original's invalid-URI path, so legitimate use is preserved.

R639.note: Placeholder plus DB::select($sql, [$region]) is the correct Laravel parameterization; query shape and JSON return are unchanged.

R640.note: vector<string_view> to vector<string> gives the cache ownership; firstLetter and the index contract are untouched (only a now-unused <string_view> include remains).

R641.note: toRealPath on base and resolved path with Path.startsWith containment closes traversal; the 404-on-missing behaviour is preserved and every added rejection path is stated.

R642.note: search(name, "(cn={0})", filterArgs, cons) applies JNDI's RFC 4515 escaping; new SearchControls() is exactly the default the original null argument selected, so scope and limits are unchanged.

R643.note: Static SecureRandom with 16 random bytes base64url-encoded replaces Math.random(); token format change is inherent and stated, and cookie/session handling is byte-for-byte the original.

R644.note: check_password() is the right API, but the stored column holds the plaintext passwords the docstring describes, so identify_hasher cannot recognise them and every legacy login now fails (or errors); the write-up asserts the opposite - that check_password 'handles both plaintext and hashed passwords' - so the required re-hash migration is never disclosed.

R645.note: crypto/rand.Read backs the key; the 36-into-256 modulo leaves a negligible bias (indices 0-3 at 8/256 vs 7/256) that does not reopen predictability, and length, alphabet, apiKeys record and 400 path are preserved.

R646.note: jwt.verify with the symmetric secret closes the forgery (v9 defaults to HS* for a string key), but next() is called inside the try, so a synchronous downstream throw is swallowed and converted into a 401 after the handler may already have responded - a behaviour change beyond the fix.

R647.note: PreparedStatement with setString(1, data) and no-arg executeQuery; declaration, result handling and all three finally close blocks are preserved.

R648.note: %q escapes CR/LF and control characters in the logged username, closing forged log lines; the only change is the quoted/escaped log rendering, which is the fix and is stated.

R649.note: Moving the session write after login_user() is a no-op: Flask-Login 0.6 only adds _user_id/_id/_fresh keys and never clears or rotates the cookie session, so pre-login attacker-planted state survives either ordering - the write-up even concedes no rotation happens; session.clear() before login_user() was needed. Nothing else changed.

R650.note: The argument array fixes the POSIX branch but not the Windows one: Java's legacy command-line assembly only quotes arguments containing space or tab, so a space-free payload like x&whoami is re-parsed by cmd.exe /c and still executes; also no -- guard against a leading dash for ls. Separately, the absolute System32 path to cmd.exe was silently replaced by a bare cmd.exe resolved through the search path.

R651.note: Content-sniffing with magic.from_buffer plus a generated uuid name closes the dangerous-upload vector, but the endpoint now rejects everything outside three MIME types (the docstring said 'PDF, DOCX, etc.') and the JSON response's filename is now the generated name instead of the caller's - both stated, but they still reject and alter previously working uploads; display_name is also computed and never used.
